title: Mushroom Fruiting
description: A slow walk through a Colorado forest floor, seen from low down, where every fruiting body is generated from its own genome. Porcini, fly agaric, shaggy mane, chanterelle, oyster, lion's mane, turkey tail, psilocybe, marasmius fairy rings, mycena (including glowing ones), xylaria, eyelash cups, wood ear, cordyceps, conks and sulphur shelves each keep their own anatomy, and an 'imaginary mushrooms' option still invents fully random species. Nothing lasts: fruits rot, dry out, deliquesce, get eaten by slugs and deer, or get picked by foragers (click one for its Latin name and what is happening to it). Dead aspens, cottonwoods, Gambel oaks, lodgepole and ponderosa pines, spruces, Douglas-firs and subalpine firs stand as snags, fall, and crumble into the soil, hosting the wood fungi as they decay. The camera drifts sideways through the woods, wind carries the spores, and fruits are spaced to avoid overlap. Scroll speed and direction, wind, spacing, grazing, foraging, dead trees, wood decay, depth mist, light, damp, variation, bioluminescence and every species switch are live and mappable. Click the ground to inoculate a flush; beats trigger a colony-wide flush.
